summary: Gurnet Light: a wooden tower on Plymouth Bay's north point, twin lights from 1768 to 1924, first kept by a woman, Hannah Thomas, and since 2026 owned by its volunteer stewards.

access.note: Reached only through private Gurnet Point; tower closed; occasional open house; keeper's cottage rentable.

stay.note: Keeper's cottage rental, sleeps up to 14

facts.agency: Project Gurnet & Bug Lights, Inc. (owner since 2026); U.S. Coast Guard maintains the aids to navigation

events.note: Legislature establishes the light; wooden dwelling with a lantern at each end completed September 1768 (LighthouseFriends)
Reported hit by shot in an engagement with HMS Niger; disputed
Brigantine General Arnold lost on White Flats
Light ceded to the United States
Keeper and assistant help mine sweeper Swan No. 34
Northeast tower removed; revolving light in remaining tower
Tower moved inland because of erosion (140 ft per LighthouseFriends; 48 ft per Plymouth Independent)
Ownership to Project Gurnet & Bug Lights under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act; deed ceremony 19 September 2026

notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the story: Hannah Thomas's last year as keeper (1786 roster, 1790 county leaflet, Hamilton's June 1790 report still names the widow, LighthouseFriends has John Thomas from 1790); Joseph Burgess end year 1851 vs 1852; Swan wreck date (27 Nov per Bulletin, 28 Nov per LighthouseFriends) and men saved (62 Commissioner vs 56 LighthouseFriends); 1998 move distance (140 ft vs 48 ft); first lighting 1768 vs 1769; lens date (USLHS and Project say 1871, LighthouseFriends says fourth-order lenses by 1879; not stated in story). Bulletin page numbers: 1932 pp. 118-119 and 1929 p. 313 taken from page markers near the text, 1929 item is OCR from interleaved columns, check the page image. Commissioner 1921 page (scan 664) printed page uncertain. The Patriot Ledger articles on the 2026 ownership could not be read (403); the Plymouth Independent piece gives 'last month' without a date, so only the Duxbury Clipper dates are used. Lover's Rock story is LighthouseFriends citing an 1896 article, unverified. Keeper roster is from the USLHS archive (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson); USCG heading lines mapped to role other. The 'Tarpaulin Cove' and Reamy other_stations come from LighthouseFriends and the 1925 Bulletin. Fort Andrew, the nearby Gurnet life-saving station (us-ma-gurnet-life-saving-station) and Duxbury Pier were not researched here. Hannah Thomas dates (born 1730/31) not used. Budget exceeded the page-read guide because the Bulletins are cached whole-volume PDFs. Fact-check 2026-10-22: ranch house date disagrees (1960 NRHP 1976 vs 1963 LighthouseFriends), now stated in the story.
